sub_sections.title: Objectives and ambition
sub_sections.content: MAESTRO — Multi-Agent Ecosystem for Strategic Task Reasoning and Orchestration — targets the fundamental limitations that prevent today's AI agents from operating reliably in real-world, high-value settings: fragile long-horizon planning, loss of coherence over extended interactions, and the absence of principled mechanisms for external tool integration and multi-agent coordination. The project pursues eight measurable objectives spanning three tightly integrated research pillars and a cross-cutting orchestration capability. OBJ-1 (Neuro-symbolic planning engine for autonomous task decomposition) targets ≥40% improvement in plan success rate over pure LLM-based baselines (ReAct, Reflexion) on standardised benchmarks (WebArena, SWE-bench, GAIA) for tasks requiring >10 sequential steps, achieved by month 36. OBJ-2 (Unified adaptive memory architecture) targets ≥30% improvement in task coherence and factual consistency over context-window-only baselines in interaction sequences exceeding 50 agent steps, achieved by month 30. OBJ-3 (Decentralised multi-agent coordination protocols) targets effective coordination of ≥5 heterogeneous agents with ≥25% improvement in joint task completion over independent agent baselines and formal proof of protocol convergence, by month 36. OBJ-4 (Healthcare demonstrator — clinical decision support) targets diagnostic reasoning accuracy within 10% of specialist clinician performance on 500 de-identified clinical cases across 5 diagnostic domains, by month 42. OBJ-5 (Manufacturing demonstrator — process optimisation) targets ≥15% reduction in defect rates and ≥10% reduction in energy consumption versus baseline operations in a pilot factory, by month 42. OBJ-6 (Logistics transfer demonstrator — cross-sector generalisation) targets ≥20% improvement in disruption recovery time and ≥15% improvement in delivery schedule adherence versus current planning systems across 3 supply chain corridors, by month 42. OBJ-8 (External Tool and API Orchestration Layer) targets a typed tool registry supporting ≥30 external tools/APIs, tool invocation success rate ≥95%, mean recovery time from tool failure ≤5s, and full provenance traces for 100% of tool invocations, by month 36. OBJ-7 (Open framework release and ecosystem contribution) targets an open-source release with ≥500 GitHub stars within 6 months of release, contributions accepted to the AI-on-demand platform, results validated through ≥2 TEFs, and technology transfer initiated through ≥3 EDIHs, by month 48. MAESTRO goes decisively beyond the state of the art by co-designing three mutually reinforcing capabilities — neuro-symbolic planning, adaptive memory, and decentralised coordination — into a unified architecture rather than combining independent research threads; this integration is not achievable from off-the-shelf components. The neuro-symbolic planning engine provides formal guarantees (verifiable sub-task decomposition, provable recovery) that pure LLM-based approaches cannot offer, while the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer treats tool integration as an architecturally central research contribution rather than a function-calling afterthought. Research activities start at TRL 2 (fundamental research on planning formalisms, memory architecture design, and coordination theory) and progress to TRL 5 (technology validated in relevant operational environments) across healthcare and advanced manufacturing, spanning the full TRL 2–5 range appropriate for a RIA.

sub_sections.title: Methodology
sub_sections.content: MAESTRO's methodology is structured around three research pillars and a cross-cutting orchestration layer, each grounded in a dedicated work package and validated through sector demonstrators. WP2 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning Engine, led by Alpenstadt Technical University) develops a hybrid planning engine that decomposes high-level goals into executable sub-task graphs with formally specified pre/post-conditions, integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search and hierarchical task networks with LLM-driven heuristic evaluation, and supports self-correction through plan monitoring and replanning from verified intermediate states — delivering D2-01 (architecture specification, month 12), D2-02 (prototype software, month 24), and D2-03 (evaluation report, month 36). WP3 (Adaptive Memory Architecture, led by Breda Institute for Intelligent Systems) implements a unified tri-store memory system integrating working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory with a learned memory controller that manages information flow, retrieval, and forgetting — delivering D3-01 (design specification, month 12), D3-02 (adaptive memory system software, month 24), and D3-03 (evaluation report, month 30). WP4 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination, led by Centre Européen de Recherche en Informatique Avancée) develops formally specified task-delegation and negotiation protocols with provable convergence guarantees, conflict resolution mechanisms, and auditable interaction traces — delivering D4-01 (protocol specification, month 12), D4-02 (software implementation, month 24), and D4-03 (coordination evaluation and audit trace report, month 36). The cross-cutting External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, developed within WP2 and WP3 with contributions from Boreal AI Labs Oy, provides a typed tool registry, formal tool selection policies, standardised API adapters for heterogeneous protocols (HL7 FHIR, OPC-UA), post-invocation verification, execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, and full provenance traces — directly addressing the call's mandatory SR-04 requirement. WP8 (Integration, Evaluation and Benchmarking, led by Fundación Ibérica de Innovación Tecnológica) integrates all pillars into the unified MAESTRO framework (D8-02, month 36), produces a community benchmark suite (D8-03, month 42), and conducts TEF-based cross-demonstrator evaluation (D8-04, month 48). Demonstrators in WP5 (healthcare, led by Nordic Institute of Health Sciences), WP6 (manufacturing, led by Istituto Superiore di Ingegneria Avanzata), and WP7 (logistics, led by EuroLog International AG) co-design validation scenarios with industry partners, apply quantitative KPIs, and provide operational deployment environments. The interdisciplinary approach combines formal methods and symbolic AI (Alpenstadt Technical University, Centre Européen de Recherche en Informatique Avancée), neural information retrieval and memory-augmented learning (Breda Institute for Intelligent Systems), clinical informatics (Nordic Institute of Health Sciences), smart manufacturing and digital twins (Istituto Superiore di Ingegneria Avanzata), logistics AI (EuroLog International AG), LLM engineering (Boreal AI Labs Oy), and AI evaluation and technology transfer (Fundación Ibérica de Innovación Tecnológica). The project is primarily technical in nature; social sciences and humanities integration is not a primary research dimension, though ethical oversight of AI agent behaviour in clinical settings is addressed through WP1 ethics compliance tasks led by Alpenstadt Technical University. The gender dimension in research content is addressed through the clinical validation design in WP5, where demographic disaggregation of diagnostic performance across the 500-case benchmark is incorporated as a KPI. Open science practices include open-source release of the MAESTRO framework (D9-02, month 36), publication of all benchmarks and datasets, and contribution of all models and results to the AI-on-demand platform; a Data Management Plan will be delivered as D9-01 (month 6) by Boreal AI Labs Oy, ensuring FAIR data principles are applied across all demonstrator datasets. Progress is monitored through 6-month integration checkpoints, standardised KPIs across all demonstrators, and the evaluation framework established in D8-01 (month 12).
